guideline: For better assess speech quality, our MOS evaluations focus on different aspects: MOS-E emphasizes the alignment of the speech with the environment description, including volume, timbre, and conveyed emotion

...We use MOS evaluations (MOS-E, MOS-C, MOS-D, MOS-S) with specific criteria such as volume appropriateness, timbre alignment, emotion conveyed, contextual adaptation, tone consistency, volume stability, timbre consistency, emotional consistency, stylistic continuity, relevance to previous turns, logical flow, turn‑taking, emotion alignment, pitch consistency, timbre alignment...

MOS evaluates the overall quality of the speech from 1 to 5, with higher scores representing better quality. Evaluators assess criteria such as clarity, emotional richness, speech speed, and relevance to contextual information.

overall_notes: This paper focuses on Text-to-Speech (TTS) research, which involves generating speech audio from text. While it is a generation task, it is specifically speech generation rather than natural language generation (text generation). Therefore, it does not fall under the scope of NLG evaluation as defined in the guidelines. The paper presents a novel TTS dataset (DNASpeech) and evaluates various TTS models, but all evaluation is focused on speech quality, not linguistic content generation.
